Surah 113 = al-Falaq (الفلق), 'The Dawn / Daybreak'; 113th in the mushaf; 5 ayat; juz 30

Al-Falaq and an-Nas together are called the 'Mu'awwidhatayn' (the two surahs of seeking refuge) - Ibn Kathir, Qurtubi, Ma'ariful Qur'an (Qurtubi also lists 'al-Muqashqishatan' - single source, not for video)

Makki/Madani: IKHTILAAF, no clear majority in opened sources. Makki: Qurtubi first view (al-Hasan, 'Ikrima, 'Ata', Jabir), Tanzil metadata 'meccan'. Madani: Ibn Kathir (Arabic text opens 'wa huma madaniyyatan' - both 113 and 114), Qurtubi's second view (one report of Ibn 'Abbas, Qatada); Ma'ariful Qur'an's cause-of-revelation (Labid in Madina) leans Madani but states no verdict; Tabari states none. Video: say 'ulama me ikhtilaaf hai' with both views
Order of revelation number: NOT found in any source opened today (Tanzil chapters has no field). Do not say a number until a PC check of an accepted list
Other names: only 'Mu'awwidhatayn' (shared with an-Nas) found. No separate second name for 113 alone in opened text

Main message: seek refuge in Allah, the Lord of the daybreak, from the evil of every created thing - the dark of night, those who tie knots with magic, the envious. Protection is with Allah alone; ('world-worry surah' - an-Nas: other side, MQ)

SHAN-E-NUZUL: the sihr (magic) incident itself is SAHIH as an event - Bukhari 5763 (Aisha: Labid bin al-A'sam of Banu Zuraiq; comb, hair, male date-palm spathe in the well of Dharwan; the Prophet went to the well, did not take revenge: 'I dislike spreading evil among people'). BUT the sahih report does NOT say these two surahs were revealed because of it. The link 'eleven ayat - eleven knots - each ayah untied a knot' comes from Ibn 'Abbas / al-Tha'labi / Qushayri-type narrations without sound isnad (Ibn Kathir: al-Tha'labi version has 'nakarah'; Ma'ariful Qur'an lists the three accounts incl. Tha'labi; Qurtubi gives it as Ibn 'Abbas account). Tabari's text has no such story. Scholars differ also because the surah is held Makki by some while Labid was in Madina. = NO sahih-grade shan-e-nuzul
facts.grade: ikhtilaaf (not sahih as cause - not for the video as fact)

facts.claim: Safe script line: 'सूरह के उतरने के बारे में तफ़्सीरों में एक रिवायत आती है कि नबी ﷺ पर जादू का असर हुआ था और इन दो सूरतों से जुड़ी बातें उसी सिलसिले में बताई जाती हैं - पर इस सूरह के उतरने की वजह वही थी, इस पर उलमा में इख़्तिलाफ़ है; सहीह रिवायत में सिर्फ़ जादू का वाक़िया है, सूरह के उतरने की वजह का ज़िक्र नहीं।' Plus the Makki/Madani ikhtilaaf line (P3). Prefer to keep it even shorter or skip the magic story entirely (sensitive).

SAHIH: the Prophet SAW said, with wonder, that verses had been sent down that night the like of which had never been seen: 'Qul a'udhu bi rabbil-falaq' and 'Qul a'udhu bi rabbin-nas' ('Uqba bin 'Amir). Muslim 814 (dataset hadithnumber 1891, arabicnumber 814.01; also Ahmad, Tirmidhi hasan sahih, Nasai - Ibn Kathir)

SAHIH (a report only, no ruling): 'A'isha - every night when going to bed the Prophet SAW joined his palms, blew into them, recited Ikhlas, Falaq and Nas, then wiped his body with them starting with head and face, three times. Bukhari 5017 (also 5748). Also in Ibn Kathir/Qurtubi (Ibn Kathir: 'Bukhari/Muslim from A'isha')

SAHIH (report only): 'A'isha - when the Prophet SAW fell ill he recited the Mu'awwidhat over himself and blew; in his last illness she recited them and wiped his hands over his body. Bukhari 5016; Muwatta Malik; Ibn Kathir, Qurtubi, Ma'ariful Qur'an

113:1 - 'Qul' = command to say; 'a'udhu' = I seek refuge/protection; 'Rabb al-falaq': Lord of the daybreak. Falaq = splitting/cleaving; most commentators (Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id bin Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatada, Jabir; Ibn Kathir says Tabari and Bukhari favour it) = the dawn/morning when it splits the dark. Wider sense (Tabari, Qurtubi): everything that Allah splits open - creation. Hell-related meanings (prison/valley/tree in Jahannam) are weakly reported and NOT used

113:2 - from the evil of what He created: all creatures' evil in general (Tabari: general; Qurtubi: all evil, some say Iblis and his offspring; Ibn Kathir: all created things). Ma'ariful: Allah is the ultimate cause of benefit and harm - protection is by sheltering with Him

113:3 - ghasiq = darkness falling; 'waqab' = enters/settles. Majority: the night when it comes with its darkness (Mujahid, Ibn 'Abbas, Qatada, al-Hasan - Ibn Kathir; al-Dahhak, al-Suddi - Qurtubi). Other views quoted: sun at sunset (al-Zuhri), a setting star/Pleiades (Ibn Zayd), the moon when it darkens/eclipses (hadith 'A'isha, Tirmidhi hasan sahih, Ahmad). Tabari: verse is general. Video: 'ज़्यादातर मुफ़स्सिरीन: अंधेरी रात जब छा जाए' + at most 'कुछ ने चाँद/तारे भी कहा'
facts.grade: maana hua (core: night); other views ikhtilaaf

facts.claim: 113:4 - al-naffathat fi al-'uqad: Mujahid, 'Ikrima, al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Dahhak (Ibn Kathir): sorceresses who blow on knotted threads while reciting; Tabari: 'al-sawahir' blowing into knots of thread; Qurtubi: female sorcerers who blow on knots (the Arabic is feminine plural). Meaning: shelter from the harm of magic. Magic is real only as Allah permits (Ma'ariful: magic works through causes; Qurtubi refers to Baqarah for sihr). Do NOT go into how magic works or fiqh on ruqya/nafth

113:5 - hasid idha hasad: the envier when he acts on his envy. Qurtubi: hasad = wishing a blessing to leave another (even if one does not gain it); the envier harms only when envy shows in word/deed; Tabari: general - any envier (disparages, wishes harm); Ibn Kathir (AR) cites Muslim 2186 'min sharri kulli hasidin wa 'ayn'. Hasad placed last to stress its harm (Qurtubi). Ghibta (wanting the same good, not its loss for the other) is different (Qurtubi, with Bukhari/Muslim 'la hasad illa fi ithnatayn' - number not opened)

Overall order of the surah: Rabb of daybreak (hope after dark) -> general evil -> darkness -> magic -> envy; Ma'ariful: dark/night mentioned because night brings harm and day removes it; Al-Falaq = worldly troubles, an-Nas = deeper/hereafter (MQ). Use only as 'tafseer ke mutabiq' lines
